items.followUp: State two properties of ionic compounds.

rubric.why: Coordinate covalent compounds generally share the physical properties of covalent compounds.
rubric.description: States that they generally have a low melting point or low boiling point.

rubric.why: They generally lack mobile charged particles that can carry an electric current.
rubric.description: States that they generally do not, or poorly, conduct electricity.

modelAnswer: Coordinate covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
They generally do not conduct electricity because they lack mobile charged particles.

items.followUp: Define the boiling point of a substance.

rubric.why: A freezing point is a temperature at which a change of state occurs.
rubric.description: Identifies the freezing point as a temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a temperature.

rubric.why: Freezing is the change of state from liquid to solid.
rubric.description: Identifies the change from liquid to solid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liquid solidifies.

modelAnswer: The freezing point is the temperature at which a liquid changes into a solid.

items.followUp: How does increasing temperature affect the rate of diffusion?

rubric.why: Strong intermolecular attractions hinder particle movement and slow diffusion.
rubric.description: Links stronger intermolecular forces with slower diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that stronger forces slow diffusion.

rubric.why: Weak intermolecular forces allow particles to move more freely and diffuse faster.
rubric.description: Links weaker intermolecular forces with faster diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that weaker forces make diffusion faster.

modelAnswer: Strong intermolecular forces hold particles together and slow their diffusion.
Weak intermolecular forces allow particles to move more freely, so diffusion is faster.

items.followUp: What is the boiling point of a liquid?

rubric.why: The melting point is a temperature at which a change of state occurs.
rubric.description: Identifies the melting point as a temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a temperature.

rubric.why: Melting is the change of state from solid to liquid.
rubric.description: Identifies the change from solid to liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solid melts.

modelAnswer: The melting point is the temperature at which a solid changes into a liquid.

items.followUp: Why do gases expand to fill their containers?

rubric.why: Gas particles are much more widely spaced than particles in liquids and solids.
rubric.description: States that gas particles are far apart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the large spaces between gas particles.

rubric.why: Widely spaced particles mean a given volume contains less matter and therefore has a lower density.
rubric.description: Connects the particle spacing to less matter per volume or lower density.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a given volume of gas has less matter or lower density.

modelAnswer: Gas particles are much farther apart than particles in liquids and solids.
Therefore, a given volume of gas contains less matter and has a lower density.
